title: Workshop
intro: Extend the workspace here: connect external MCP servers and APIs, and choose which agent may use them. Secrets are stored encrypted; agents never see them.
notFound: The owner and the admins see this page.

connectors.emptyBody: Connect an MCP server (e.g. Jira, GitHub), and the agents you allow can use its tools.
connectors.noKeys: The server has no encryption key (COLONY_SECRET_KEYS), so connectors that need a secret cannot be added now. Ask the server's owner to set it.
connectors.approvalLabel: Write and external calls without approval
connectors.approvalHint: Only the owner can switch it off. When off, agents write and send data through this connector without a person's approval.
connectors.noTools: No tools (extensions give an HTTP API its tools).
connectors.deleteBody: Its secret and every grant to it are deleted; agents no longer reach its tools. The call log stays.
connectors.riskHint: Calls of tools that write or send data out ask for approval. Only the owner can lower a risk.

dialog.name: Name
dialog.slugHint: Agents see its tools as {{slug}}__tool. 2–16 lower-case letters, digits or _.
dialog.slugBad: 2–16 characters: lower-case letters, digits and _, starting with a letter, without __.
dialog.urlHint: A public https address. The server's owner can allow internal addresses (COLONY_EGRESS_ALLOW).
dialog.secretHint: Stored encrypted and never shown again. The server puts it on the requests; agents do not see it.

grants.intro: An agent sees only the connectors it has a grant for.
grants.noAgents: There are no agents in the workspace.
grants.noConnectors: Add a connector or an extension first.

calls.intro: Who called which tool, when, how long it took and how it ended. The calls' content is never kept here.

extensions.emptyBody: An extension gives agents tools of your own: an HTTP call to a connector, or your own JavaScript/TypeScript code. Every extension gets its own bot, so what it does stays traceable.
extensions.noRunner: The server has no code runner (COLONY_EXT_RUNNER_URL), so JavaScript tools do not run now; HTTP tools do.
extensions.approvalLabel: Write and external tools without approval
extensions.approvalHint: Only the owner can switch it off.
extensions.takeOverHint: When the maintainer is no longer an admin, the extension does not run until someone takes it over.
extensions.deleteBody: Its grants are revoked and its bot archived. The versions and the call log stay.
extensions.title: Name
extensions.slugHint: Agents see its tools as x_{{slug}}__tool.
extensions.botHandleHint: The extension writes and calls under this name; it does not change later. Default x-{{slug}}.
extensions.manifestHint: Tools (name, kind: js or http, risk, input), connectors, allowed outbound hosts (egress), store collections. See docs/25, 13.4.
extensions.manifestBad: The manifest is not a valid JSON object.
extensions.sourceHint: Every exported function is a tool: (input, ctx). ctx has fetch, store, colony, call, log.
extensions.saved: Saved: v{{version}}. Before it goes live, look at what it adds and test it.
extensions.diff: What it adds compared with the live version
extensions.diffCode: The code or the requests changed.
extensions.testHint: A test is a real call as the extension's bot; it asks no approval and is logged as a test.

routines.webhookOnce: The {{routine}} routine's webhook address (shown only now; the old one stopped working):
